verdict.rationale: Homebrew's Brewfile mechanism (docs-1/13/20/37, docs-30/31) lets a project declare which packages/taps to install and can restore installed state via brew bundle install, but it records package names/taps rather than enforcing exact version pins, and Homebrew formulae generally always install the latest available version. Community evidence directly contradicts the pinning story: users report being 'screwed too many times on mandatory upgrades I couldn't pin' and switching to mise for arbitrary version installs (homebrew-comm-5, homebrew-comm-6), and another explicitly wants 'a standard Homebrew way to install multiple versions of node, php and Python' because none exists (homebrew-comm-9). missing for 10: documented exact-version pinning syntax in Brewfile, evidence that brew bundle install respects a specified version rather than latest, and confirmation that upgrades won't override a pinned version.
